executive_summary: Oslo's GOP ran 5.4% ahead of Budget in February, but that beat is not fully organic — it traces substantially to a Utilities shortfall that looks like a missing invoice rather than a genuine saving. Worth flagging to the GM before this reads as a clean win.
profitability_summary: GOP came in at 2,966,278 NOK, 5.4% (151,409 NOK) ahead of Budget of 2,814,869 NOK. Most of that beat traces to Utilities running well under Budget this month — see the Utilities note below before reading this as a clean win on cost control.

category_narratives.utilities: Utilities landed at 391,068 NOK against a Budget of 491,144 NOK — 20.4% under. Confirm the February electricity invoice was actually received and posted: the drill-down shows only a 5,267 NOK "estimated accrual" for Electricity this month, while every other utilities account (heating, water, waste, fuel) is running at its normal level. A gap this size, concentrated in a single account, usually means the invoice hasn't arrived yet rather than genuine savings — expect this to reverse, and likely overshoot, once it's billed.
category_narratives.gop: GOP beat Budget by 5.4% (151,409 NOK), but the Utilities shortfall above accounts for most of it. On a normalized basis — adding back the missing utilities charge — the underlying beat is closer to flat. Worth keeping in mind before this reads as a clean operational win.
category_narratives.ebitda: Follows GOP's favorable variance for the same reason — the Utilities timing gap flows straight through. Not an independent story.
category_narratives.ebit: Same driver as GOP/EBITDA above — no separate action needed here.
category_narratives.pretax_income: Same driver as GOP/EBITDA/EBIT above — no separate action needed here.
